summary: Martian Map is a browser-based EVA planning HUD for Jezero Crater (18.38 N, 77.58 E), built by team Tuxonauts for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge (Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map). Existing global Mars viewers display orbital imagery and elevation without connecting them to spacesuit life-support limits or solar event alerts. Our application puts NASA Mars Trek Viking and MOLA layers, a historical CTX orbital mosaic, simulated suit oxygen and battery budgets, an optional radiation dose cap, and NASA DONKI space weather notices into one screen. Users can place a surface target to check an illustrative 96-vertex geodesic return envelope, inspect a local crater-rim science destination with a four-segment detour around a project-defined crater exclusion, and toggle Pressurized Glove Mode for larger, high-contrast controls.
details:
Martian Map centers on a Habitat Base marker at Jezero Crater (18.38 N, 77.58 E) inside a Leaflet map initialized with L.CRS.EPSG4326 equirectangular display coordinates. The layer switcher changes between four views while keeping the current map center, active target, and suit reserves intact:

- OPTICAL: NASA Mars Trek Viking MDIM21 global color mosaic at 232 m/px (maxNativeZoom 7).

- ELEVATION: NASA Mars Trek MGS MOLA colorized shaded relief at 463 m/px (maxNativeZoom 6).

- BLENDED: Viking optical mosaic with the MOLA relief layer overlaid at 0.55 opacity.

- CTX Detail: Historical MRO Context Camera (CTX) beta01 orbital mosaic at roughly 5 m/px (hosted by Esri, capped at service level 12 / maxNativeZoom 13). Viking stays active underneath as a fallback, and each CTX tile request enforces a 15-second timeout plus PNG header and IEND trailer checks so truncated tiles do not render as blank squares.

The EVA model in src/evaModel.js calculates an illustrative round-trip return perimeter using demonstration suit assumptions: 240 minutes of oxygen at 100%, 180 minutes of battery at 100%, a 2,000 m/h walking speed, and a 20 percentage point protected reserve taken off full capacity (yielding 144 minutes of excursion time and a 2,400 m direct radius at full reserves). The map draws this perimeter as a 96-vertex spherical geodesic polygon using the Mars sphere radius of 3,396,190 m (GCS_Mars_2000_Sphere). Clicking the map or pressing "Use map center" places a target and compares unrounded haversine distance against the return radius, reporting round-trip time, signed time margin, and the limiting resource.

For local mission context, src/scienceData.js defines "East crater survey" (18.367767 N, 77.619095 E), an observation point derived from CTX imagery. Users can compare a straight-line estimate against a four-segment detour north of a 13-point project-defined crater exclusion contour. Segment validation checks that every waypoint stays inside the local review window and clear of the exclusion polygon before displaying travel times.

Under the Simplified model panel, an opt-in Radiation simulation applies a constant Low (0.10 mSv/h) or High (0.50 mSv/h) dose rate against an adjustable 0 to 0.30 mSv demo allowance, tightening the excursion budget when radiation becomes the limiting factor. Independently, the Space weather panel queries https://api.nasa.gov/DONKI/notifications for CME notices over the past seven UTC calendar days, validates timestamps and CCMC links, deduplicates by messageID, and falls back to the historical NASA record 20240510-AL-003 (2024-05-10 13:38 UTC) if the API is unreachable. DONKI notices provide space weather context only and do not measure surface radiation on Mars.

Toggling "Glove mode" in the header switches the interface to Pressurized Glove Mode, applying opaque #020617 panels, 44 px minimum touch targets, #22D3EE active borders, and #FACC15 focus outlines designed for stiff spacesuit gloves.

Tech stack: React 19, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS v4, and Leaflet 1.9.4, with inline SVGs and no external icon or state libraries.

Source repository: https://github.com/marcosschlick/martian-map
